1.Why FLOPs alone cannot explain LLM latency#

When engineers optimize deep learning models solely by counting floating-point operations (FLOPs), two paradoxes appear immediately:

  1. Autoregressive generation is orders of magnitude slower per token than prompt prefill, even though the per-token linear algebra executes the exact same matrix weights.
  2. Standard self-attention spends most of its wall-clock time waiting on memory, even when the GPU's Tensor Cores are less than 25%25\%25% utilized.

Both phenomena are governed by the Roofline Model, which relates an operator's Arithmetic Intensity (I=FLOPs/Bytes transferred\mathcal{I} = \text{FLOPs} / \text{Bytes transferred}I=FLOPs/Bytes transferred) to the hardware's Ridge Point:

Iridge=Peak Compute Throughput (FLOPs/s)Peak HBM Bandwidth (Bytes/s)\mathcal{I}_{\text{ridge}} = \frac{\text{Peak Compute Throughput (FLOPs/s)}}{\text{Peak HBM Bandwidth (Bytes/s)}}Iridge​=Peak HBM Bandwidth (Bytes/s)Peak Compute Throughput (FLOPs/s)​
(1)

For an NVIDIA H100 SXM GPU delivering 989 TFLOPS989\text{ TFLOPS}989 TFLOPS of dense bfloat16 Tensor Core compute and 3.35 TB/s3.35\text{ TB/s}3.35 TB/s (3350 GB/s3350\text{ GB/s}3350 GB/s) of HBM3 bandwidth, the ridge point is:

IridgeH100=989×1012 FLOPs/s3350×109 Bytes/s≈295.2 FLOPs/Byte\mathcal{I}_{\text{ridge}}^{\text{H100}} = \frac{989 \times 10^{12}\text{ FLOPs/s}}{3350 \times 10^{9}\text{ Bytes/s}} \approx \mathbf{295.2\text{ FLOPs/Byte}}IridgeH100​=3350×109 Bytes/s989×1012 FLOPs/s​≈295.2 FLOPs/Byte
(2)

Any kernel with arithmetic intensity below 295.2 FLOPs/Byte295.2\text{ FLOPs/Byte}295.2 FLOPs/Byte is Memory-bound (bottlenecked by HBM3 bandwidth); any kernel above it is Compute-bound (bottlenecked by Tensor Core math pipes).

2.The Prefill versus Decode arithmetic intensity ledger#

Using our first-principles calculator (labs/llm/roofline-flash), let us evaluate Llama-3-8B (N=8.03BN = 8.03\text{B}N=8.03B parameters, 15.0 GB15.0\text{ GB}15.0 GB in bfloat16) at sequence length S=4096S = 4096S=4096 across batch sizes B∈{1,16,128}B \in \{1, 16, 128\}B∈{1,16,128}:

  • Prefill Phase (B×SB \times SB×S tokens processed in parallel): Every weight matrix is loaded once from HBM and multiplied against B×SB \times SB×S token vectors via dense GEMM:
Iprefill≈2NBS2N+BytesKV(B,S)\mathcal{I}_{\text{prefill}} \approx \frac{2 N B S}{2 N + \text{Bytes}_{\text{KV}}(B, S)}Iprefill​≈2N+BytesKV​(B,S)2NBS​
(3)
  • Decode Phase (B×1B \times 1B×1 new tokens generated per step): Every single decoding step must reload all 2N2N2N bytes of model weights plus all B×SB \times SB×S historical KV cache vectors from HBM just to compute BBB token outputs:
Idecode≈2NB2N+BytesKV(B,S)≤B FLOPs/Byte\mathcal{I}_{\text{decode}} \approx \frac{2 N B}{2 N + \text{Bytes}_{\text{KV}}(B, S)} \le B\text{ FLOPs/Byte}Idecode​≈2N+BytesKV​(B,S)2NB​≤B FLOPs/Byte
(4)

@dataclass
class GPUConfig:
    name: str
    fp16_tflops: float
    hbm_bandwidth_gbps: float
    vram_gb: float

    @property
    def ridge_point(self) -> float:
        return (self.fp16_tflops * 1e12) / (self.hbm_bandwidth_gbps * 1e9)


H100_SXM = GPUConfig("NVIDIA H100 SXM (80GB)", fp16_tflops=989.0, hbm_bandwidth_gbps=3350.0, vram_gb=80.0)


@dataclass
class ModelLedger:
    name: str
    num_layers: int
    hidden_size: int
    num_q_heads: int
    num_kv_heads: int
    head_dim: int
    intermediate_size: int
    vocab_size: int
    mla_kv_lora_rank: int = 0

    def total_params(self) -> int:
        emb = 2 * self.vocab_size * self.hidden_size
        attn = self.hidden_size * (2 * self.num_q_heads + 2 * self.num_kv_heads) * self.head_dim
        ffn = 3 * self.hidden_size * self.intermediate_size
        norm = 2 * self.hidden_size
        return emb + self.num_layers * (attn + ffn + norm)

    def kv_cache_bytes(self, batch_size: int, seq_len: int, bytes_per_elem: int = 2) -> int:
        if self.mla_kv_lora_rank > 0:
            return self.num_layers * batch_size * seq_len * self.mla_kv_lora_rank * bytes_per_elem
        return 2 * self.num_layers * batch_size * seq_len * self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim * bytes_per_elem

    def arithmetic_intensity(self, batch_size: int, seq_len: int) -> dict[str, float]:
        params = self.total_params()
        weight_bytes = params * 2
        kv_bytes = self.kv_cache_bytes(batch_size, seq_len)
        prefill_ai = (2.0 * params * batch_size * seq_len) / (weight_bytes + kv_bytes)
        decode_ai = (2.0 * params * batch_size) / (weight_bytes + kv_bytes)
        return {"prefill_flops_per_byte": prefill_ai, "decode_flops_per_byte": decode_ai}

At B=1B = 1B=1, decoding achieves 0.97 FLOPs/Byte0.97\text{ FLOPs/Byte}0.97 FLOPs/Byte—leaving 99.6%99.6\%99.6% of the H100's Tensor Cores idle while waiting on HBM reads. Even when batching B=128B = 128B=128 concurrent requests, the growing KV cache denominator prevents decode intensity from crossing the 295.2 FLOPs/Byte295.2\text{ FLOPs/Byte}295.2 FLOPs/Byte ridge point.

3.FlashAttention: IO-aware SRAM tiling and Online Softmax#

During training and long-context prefill, the linear projections are compute-bound, but self-attention itself is severely memory-bound. Given Q,K,V∈RN×dQ, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}Q,K,V∈RN×d in HBM, standard attention executes three separate kernel stages:

  1. Read Q,KQ, KQ,K from HBM, compute S=QK⊤/d∈RN×NS = QK^\top / \sqrt{d} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}S=QK⊤/d​∈RN×N, and write SSS back to HBM (O(N2)O(N^2)O(N2) writes).
  2. Read SSS from HBM, compute P=Softmax⁡(S)∈RN×NP = \operatorname{Softmax}(S) \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}P=Softmax(S)∈RN×N, and write PPP back to HBM (O(N2)O(N^2)O(N2) reads and writes).
  3. Read PPP and VVV from HBM, compute O=PV∈RN×dO = PV \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}O=PV∈RN×d, and write OOO to HBM.

At N=32768N = 32768N=32768, B=4B = 4B=4, and H=32H = 32H=32 heads, materializing SSS and PPP transfers over 1,024 GB1,024\text{ GB}1,024 GB of intermediate HBM traffic per layer! Yet each Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) on an A100/H100 has fast on-chip SRAM (192 KB–256 KB192\text{ KB}\text{--}256\text{ KB}192 KB–256 KB per SM) operating at ∼19 TB/s\sim 19\text{ TB/s}∼19 TB/s—nearly 6×6\times6× faster than HBM3.

Dao et al. (FlashAttention, arXiv:2205.14135[1][1] · FlashAttention-1 · 2022FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-AwarenessOpen arXiv:2205.14135 ↗) fused all three steps into a single CUDA kernel by tiling QQQ into blocks Qi∈RBr×dQ_i \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times d}Qi​∈RBr​×d in SRAM and streaming blocks Kj,Vj∈RBc×dK_j, V_j \in \mathbb{R}^{B_c \times d}Kj​,Vj​∈RBc​×d across them. The mathematical obstacle is that Softmax couples every column in a row through its global maximum m(x)=max⁡kxkm(x) = \max_k x_km(x)=maxk​xk​ and denominator ℓ(x)=∑kexk−m(x)\ell(x) = \sum_k e^{x_k - m(x)}ℓ(x)=∑k​exk​−m(x).

Online Softmax resolves this by maintaining a running row maximum mi(j)m_i^{(j)}mi(j)​ and a rescaled running sum ℓi(j)\ell_i^{(j)}ℓi(j)​ as each key/value tile jjj arrives in SRAM:

minew=max⁡ ⁣(miold, rowmax⁡(Sij)),αi=exp⁡ ⁣(miold−minew)m_i^{\text{new}} = \max\!\big(m_i^{\text{old}},\, \operatorname{rowmax}(S_{ij})\big), \qquad \alpha_i = \exp\!\big(m_i^{\text{old}} - m_i^{\text{new}}\big)minew​=max(miold​,rowmax(Sij​)),αi​=exp(miold​−minew​)
(5)
ℓinew=αiℓiold+rowsum⁡ ⁣(exp⁡(Sij−minew)),O~inew=αiO~iold+exp⁡(Sij−minew)Vj\ell_i^{\text{new}} = \alpha_i \ell_i^{\text{old}} + \operatorname{rowsum}\!\Big(\exp(S_{ij} - m_i^{\text{new}})\Big), \qquad \tilde{O}_i^{\text{new}} = \alpha_i \tilde{O}_i^{\text{old}} + \exp(S_{ij} - m_i^{\text{new}}) V_jℓinew​=αi​ℓiold​+rowsum(exp(Sij​−minew​)),O~inew​=αi​O~iold​+exp(Sij​−minew​)Vj​
(6)

Suppose after processing tiles 1…j−11 \dots j-11…j−1, our unnormalized output accumulator satisfies O~i(j−1)=∑t<jexp⁡(Sit−mi(j−1))Vt\tilde{O}_i^{(j-1)} = \sum_{t < j} \exp(S_{it} - m_i^{(j-1)}) V_tO~i(j−1)​=∑t<j​exp(Sit​−mi(j−1)​)Vt​. When tile jjj updates the row maximum from mi(j−1)m_i^{(j-1)}mi(j−1)​ to mi(j)m_i^{(j)}mi(j)​, multiplying O~i(j−1)\tilde{O}_i^{(j-1)}O~i(j−1)​ by αi=exp⁡(mi(j−1)−mi(j))\alpha_i = \exp(m_i^{(j-1)} - m_i^{(j)})αi​=exp(mi(j−1)​−mi(j)​) uses the exponential law ea⋅eb=ea+be^a \cdot e^b = e^{a+b}ea⋅eb=ea+b:

After the final tile completes, dividing O~i\tilde{O}_iO~i​ by ℓi\ell_iℓi​ yields the exact full-sequence attention output Oi=Softmax⁡(Si)VO_i = \operatorname{Softmax}(S_i) VOi​=Softmax(Si​)V without ever writing SSS or PPP to HBM. Furthermore, during backpropagation, FlashAttention avoids storing the O(N2)O(N^2)O(N2) matrices by saving only the compact log-sum-exp vector Li=mi+log⁡ℓi∈RNL_i = m_i + \log \ell_i \in \mathbb{R}^NLi​=mi​+logℓi​∈RN and recomputing attention tiles on-chip in SRAM.

def tiled_flash_attention(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, block_size: int = 16) -> Tensor:
    """
    Exact blockwise attention using Online Softmax rescaling without materializing the N x N matrix.
    Shapes: q, k, v of shape [B, H, N, D].
    """
    b, h, n, d = q.shape
    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(d)
    out = torch.zeros_like(q, dtype=torch.float32)

    for i_start in range(0, n, block_size):
        i_end = min(i_start + block_size, n)
        q_block = q[:, :, i_start:i_end, :].float()  # [B, H, Br, D]
        br = i_end - i_start

        m_i = torch.full((b, h, br, 1), float("-inf"), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
        l_i = torch.zeros((b, h, br, 1), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
        acc_o = torch.zeros((b, h, br, d), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)

        q_pos = torch.arange(i_start, i_end, device=q.device)[:, None]

        for j_start in range(0, i_end, block_size):
            j_end = min(j_start + block_size, n)
            k_block = k[:, :, j_start:j_end, :].float()
            v_block = v[:, :, j_start:j_end, :].float()
            k_pos = torch.arange(j_start, j_end, device=q.device)[None, :]

            scores = (q_block @ k_block.transpose(-2, -1)) * scale
            scores = scores.masked_fill(k_pos > q_pos, float("-inf"))

            block_max = scores.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
            m_new = torch.maximum(m_i, block_max)
            # Rescale previous accumulator and denominator to the new running maximum m_new.
            alpha = torch.exp(m_i - m_new)
            p_tilde = torch.exp(scores - m_new)

            l_i = alpha * l_i + p_tilde.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
            acc_o = alpha * acc_o + (p_tilde @ v_block)
            m_i = m_new

        out[:, :, i_start:i_end, :] = acc_o / l_i

    return out.to(q.dtype)

4.FlashAttention-2: Loop inversion and warp partitioning#

While FlashAttention-1 eliminated O(N2)O(N^2)O(N2) HBM traffic, it achieved only 25%–40%25\%\text{--}40\%25%–40% of theoretical peak FLOPs on A100. FlashAttention-2 (Dao, arXiv:2307.08691[2][2] · FlashAttention-2 · 2023FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work PartitioningOpen arXiv:2307.08691 ↗) identified three GPU microarchitectural bottlenecks and fixed them:

  1. Inverting the outer and inner loops: FlashAttention-1 placed K,VK, VK,V blocks in the outer loop and QQQ blocks in the inner loop, forcing every inner step to read and atomically accumulate partial updates to OiO_iOi​ and ℓi\ell_iℓi​ in HBM. FlashAttention-2 moves QiQ_iQi​ to the outer loop and streams Kj,VjK_j, V_jKj​,Vj​ in the inner loop so the accumulator O~i\tilde{O}_iO~i​ stays entirely inside registers/SRAM for the full lifetime of the loop.
  2. Warp partitioning (Split-QQQ over Split-KKK): Instead of splitting KKK across 4 warps in a threadblock (which requires shared-memory barrier synchronization after every GEMM to sum QKj⊤Q K_j^\topQKj⊤​), FlashAttention-2 assigns disjoint rows of QiQ_iQi​ to each warp. Every warp streams the shared Kj,VjK_j, V_jKj​,Vj​ tiles from SRAM with zero inter-warp communication.
  3. Causal block skipping: For any tile where all column indices exceed all row indices (jstart>iendj_{\text{start}} > i_{\text{end}}jstart​>iend​), the entire block is skipped instead of computing and masking zeros, saving nearly 50%50\%50% of causal attention FLOPs.

5.PagedAttention (vLLM): Virtual memory for the KV cache#

Even with GQA and FlashAttention-2, production serving engines wasted 60%–80%60\%\text{--}80\%60%–80% of GPU memory on KV cache fragmentation. Because an LLM's output length is unknown ahead of time, early serving frameworks pre-allocated a contiguous HBM slab of size Smax⁡S_{\max}Smax​ (e.g., 409640964096 or 327683276832768 tokens) for every active request. This caused three forms of waste:

  • Internal fragmentation: Reserved slots for future tokens that a short completion never uses.
  • Reservation waste: Slots held idle while waiting for future decoding steps.
  • External fragmentation: Contiguous slabs of varying sequence lengths cannot pack cleanly into HBM.

Kwon et al. (vLLM / PagedAttention, arXiv:2309.06180[3][3] · vLLM / PagedAttention · 2023Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttentionOpen arXiv:2309.06180 ↗) mapped operating-system virtual memory directly onto the KV cache:

  1. Fixed-size physical KV blocks: HBM is partitioned into small, uniform physical pages (e.g., Bblock=16B_{\text{block}} = 16Bblock​=16 tokens per block).
  2. Logical-to-physical Page Table: Each sequence appends to logical blocks on demand; a block table maps logical block IDs to non-contiguous physical HBM blocks, driving internal fragmentation below 4%4\%4% (at most 151515 unused token slots at the tail of a sequence).
  3. Copy-on-Write (CoW) prefix sharing: When multiple requests share a system prompt or conduct parallel sampling (n>1n > 1n>1), their page tables point to the exact same physical KV blocks with reference counting. Only when a branch mutates a partially filled block does vLLM allocate a new physical page and copy those 16 tokens.
